exposure: Circadian rhythm (operationalized as morning vs. afternoon C-section timing)
cohort: The study included women undergoing elective cesarean delivery with spinal anesthesia, excluding those with inadequate anesthesia or major comorbidities.
finding: The overall incidence of hypotension was 66%, with severe hypotension occurring at a significantly higher rate in the morning group (43%) compared to the afternoon group (30.2%) during spinal anesthesia for cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: The timing of cesarean delivery (morning vs. afternoon) was found to influence the incidence of spinal anesthesia-induced hypotension.
